updateCadence: Follows Firefox ESR with delays; releases distributed mainly via GNU Guix
summary: A de-branded Firefox ESR rebuild by GNU: ships LibreJS, HTTPS Everywhere-style defaults and only free-software add-ons, but official binaries come mainly via Guix and distro packages and updates lag.
bestFor: GNU/Linux users who want Firefox without proprietary pieces

pros.title: Fully free software
pros.detail: No proprietary components or non-free add-on recommendations.

pros.title: Gecko compatibility
pros.detail: Inherits Firefox ESR web compatibility and MV2 add-on support.

cons.title: Slow updates
cons.detail: Based on ESR 140; latest 140.11.0 is from May 2026.

cons.title: Poor distribution
cons.detail: Official releases mostly via GNU Guix; other builds are third-party.

cons.title: No DRM
cons.detail: Lacks Widevine and easy media DRM.

faq.a: Official releases are distributed through GNU Guix; Trisquel, Parabola and Fedora package it, and Windows/macOS builds are unofficial.
Latest found is 140.11.0 (May 18, 2026) on ESR 140, which trails the current Firefox ESR 153.

faq.q: Is it the same as Firefox?
faq.a: It is Firefox ESR with proprietary bits and tracking removed.

switching.note: Imports from other browsers like Firefox.

spec.patchSpeed: Lags upstream ESR by weeks to months
